title: Keplr social-login private-key exposure and unauthorized transfers
notes: The existing Keplr entity remains active. The affected boundary is the Web3Auth-dependent Google/Apple account variant rather than a particular Keplr client release. No product-specific impact or final reimbursement outcome is established. Torus Wallet is also named in the provider's update; its separate identity and product boundary require separate review. Direct retrieval of some links was unavailable; the official November 13 statement was available as indexed full text. Review primary links and run candidate validation before canonical promotion.

affected_variants: Accounts created with Google or Apple login via Web3Auth
events.title: Web3Auth security incident exposed some Keplr social-login wallet keys
events.description: Keplr reported unauthorized transactions involving some accounts created using Google or Apple login and paused those login options. Web3Auth confirmed a security issue in its own infrastructure affecting certain embedded wallets. Keplr distinguished recovery-phrase and hardware-wallet accounts from the affected social-login variant. Web3Auth and Keplr moved at-risk assets into protective recovery wallets. On November 13 Web3Auth reported that access for existing users of its Plug & Play and SFA SDKs had resumed, with restrictions remaining, and that return of recovered assets was still being coordinated.
events.affected_users_text: Some Google/Apple-login accounts; Keplr co-founder estimated approximately 20% of this cohort, not 20% of all users (reported by The Block).
events.amount_text: Bitquery estimated USD 1.82 million taken by the attacker; The Block reported about USD 5.6 million held at published recovery addresses on November 8. These are distinct estimates, not an official final loss or reimbursement total.
events.notes: November 7 is the provider's confirmed disclosure date, not the date of the earliest unauthorized transaction. Bitquery reported earlier activity beginning November 1 UTC. No confirmed specific Keplr client version, technical root cause, final loss, victim count, return completion or Keplr-specific full restoration. Protective transfers are not counted as theft; SDK service restoration does not establish that compromised keys are safe. Initial Keplr guidance instructed affected users not to fund or recreate the old account.

evidence.title: Update on the Web3Auth Security Incident: Service Restoration and Asset Recovery
evidence.notes: Indexed full first-party text confirms November 7 infrastructure issue; names Keplr and Torus Wallet, explains protective recovery and pending returns, and distinguishes restored existing-user access from remaining registration restrictions.

evidence.title: Web3Auth says it frontran hackers by moving $5.6 million out of exposed Keplr wallets
evidence.notes: Reports key exposure, Keplr co-founder estimate for the social-login cohort, and snapshot value of published protective recovery addresses.

evidence.title: Keplr Wallet Hack: Attacker Took $1.82M Before the Rescue
evidence.notes: Independent on-chain reconstruction with data read on November 12; estimated theft is distinct from protective transfers and not a final provider-confirmed total.

evidence.notes: First-party help explicitly documents Web3Auth dependency for Google login and distinguishes Ledger and local private-key handling.

evidence.notes: Secondary report reproduces initial vendor instructions and links the Keplr official announcement at https://x.com/keplrwallet/status/2118933132900802826; direct original permalink requires review.
